questions.q: Describe the different modes of transport and their relative advantages.
answer: Transport, the movement of people and goods from place to place, uses land, water and air, each with its own strengths.

answer.text: Roads are flexible and provide door-to-door service, ideal for short distances and hilly terrain. Railways carry heavy and bulky goods and large numbers of passengers over long distances at low cost. Pipelines efficiently move liquids and gases such as oil and natural gas.

Water transport, by inland waterways and ocean routes, is the cheapest means of carrying heavy and bulky goods over long distances, though it is slow. Great canals such as the Suez and the Panama have shortened world sea routes.
Air transport is the fastest but the most expensive mode. It is valuable for long distances, for reaching difficult terrain, and for carrying perishable or high-value goods.

answer: Thus each mode suits particular goods and distances, and together they knit the world's economy.

questions.q: Why is international trade important, and what determines the balance of trade of a country?

answer.text: is the exchange of goods and services between countries, and it is important for prosperity and development.

list: It lets countries buy what they cannot produce well and sell what they produce best (comparative advantage)
It gives consumers more choice and producers larger markets, and earns foreign exchange
It is the difference between the value of a country's exports and imports of goods
A favourable balance means exports exceed imports; an unfavourable one means imports exceed exports, which must be financed

questions.q: What role do ports and international organisations play in world trade?

answer.text: depends on the physical means to move goods and on rules to govern exchange, so ports and international organisations are both vital.

list: Most international trade moves by sea, so ports handle the loading, unloading and storage of goods
They link a country's producers and consumers to world markets
The World Trade Organization frames and enforces rules for fair trade among nations
It settles trade disputes and works to reduce barriers, helping trade flow smoothly
